en.headline: Private secondary schools rise 56 per cent in five years
en.dek: The Education Bureau said the number of private secondary schools grew from 16 to 25 between 2021-22 and 2025-26, citing a stronger economy and changing parental preferences.
body: The number of private secondary schools in Hong Kong has increased by more than half over five years, according to Education Bureau figures. The count rose from 16 in the 2021-22 academic year to 25 in 2025-26, a rise of 56.3 per cent.

The bureau attributed the growth to a stronger economy and shifting parental preferences. School leaders said demand for alternative curricula had risen, and that more mainland Chinese and overseas students were considering Hong Kong universities because of their improving global rankings and amid geopolitical concerns.

Over the same period the number of private primary schools rose more modestly, from 62 to 65, an increase of 4.8 per cent. New operators have been seeking to attract families drawn by the city’s highly ranked universities, the bureau and school principals said.

zh.headline: 私營中學五年間增逾五成 教育局指經濟及家長偏好轉變
zh.dek: 教育局數字顯示，私營中學由2021-22學年的16間增至2025-26學年的25間，增幅達56.3%。
body: 香港私營中學數目在五年間增加逾一半。教育局數字顯示，由2021-22學年的16間，升至2025-26學年的25間，增幅達56.3%。
教育局把增長歸因於經濟改善及家長偏好轉變。校方負責人表示，家長對另類課程的需求上升，而香港大學的全球排名改善，加上地緣政治因素，亦令更多內地及海外學生考慮來港升學。
同期私營小學數目由62間增至65間，升幅較為溫和，僅4.8%。教育局及校長指出，新營辦商正試圖吸引被本港高排名大學吸引的家庭。
